expected: We believe an effort forecast built by resampling a team's own past forecast errors (Monte Carlo over the ratio of actual to forecast) gives ranges a team can plan with, unlike a range built by adding up every part's best and worst case. Tested forward in time on TerraQuotes' delivery ledger: each issue is forecast using only the issues finished before it.

We believe a range read straight from a team's own past misses, interpolating between them at the (n+1) positions in log space, covers about 80% of actuals at every history size from ten items up. The current forecaster's 4,000 resampled draws cover only about 70% to 77% of actuals when a team has 10 to 30 finished items, because a bootstrap of a short history under-reaches its tails. That made the README's trust rule ("coverage should sit near 0.8") raise false alarms for exactly the teams just starting.  Chosen after an exploratory simulation, run before this prediction, which compared five methods on lognormal, heavy-tailed and TerraQuotes-resampled histories of 9 to 100 items.
